case_title: Sham @ Kishor Bhaskarrao Matkari v. State of Maharashtra
accused_occupation: Unemployed (described as jobless at the time of the incident)
previous_criminal_record: No (antecedents described as unblemished; no prior criminal activity shown)
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (brother of the deceased; victims included the brother, his wife, their children)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 (murder); IPC s.307 (attempt to murder); IPC s.201 (charged; trial court acquitted on s.201)
weapon: Large stone and gas cylinder with tube found near the body; court stated no dangerous weapon was used
evidence_type: Eyewitness (child witness PW-7 and neighbour/landlord PWs 1 and 3); medical (post-mortem doctors PWs 6 and 11); recovery (stone inside house); confessional statement recorded by Executive Magistrate
confession: Confessional statement made in hospital to Executive Magistrate (treated as s.164 CrPC statement); relied on by the Court
aggravating_circumstances: Per the High Court's findings recited by the Supreme Court: three deaths, two children injured, midnight attack on sleeping and defenceless victims, gas used on wife, false intruder story, brutality towards children
mitigating_circumstances: Quarrel arose from land/property dispute; no premeditation or pre-plan; no dangerous weapon used; accused was sleeping in same house as victims; unblemished antecedents; accused was 28 and jobless; long custody (over 10 years in jail, over 5 in death cell)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC: life imprisonment and Rs.25,000 fine (default 2 years RI); convicted under s.307 IPC: 7 years RI and Rs.1,000 fine (default 3 months RI); acquitted under s.201 IPC
high_court_outcome: Accused's appeal dismissed; State's appeal allowed; conviction upheld; life sentence enhanced to death
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 (conviction maintained); IPC s.307 conviction also upheld as agreed in para 10
neutral_facts: The accused lived in a rented house with the victim (the accused's brother), the victim's wife, and their three children. On the evening before the incident, a quarrel took place between the accused and the victim inside the house, and the accused said the victim would be dealt with later. In the early hours of the following morning, a neighbour living in an adjoining tenancy heard shouting from the victim's house, the wife's cries, sounds of beating and a child groaning, and noticed a smell of gas leakage and something burning. The neighbour and the landlord went towards the house and met the accused coming out; the accused's hands and clothes were stained with blood, and the accused said three thieves had entered and assaulted the family. Smoke was seen coming from the house and the police were called. Officers found the accused with a bleeding head injury and took the accused to hospital. Inside the house, the victim and the wife were found dead; the wife was partly burnt, and a large stone and a gas cylinder with tube lay near her body. One son was found injured, died later, and two other children were injured. A spot panchanama was drawn and a wooden rafter with bloodstains and a large stone were seized. Post-mortem doctors recorded injuries on the deceased. While in hospital, the accused made a statement to an Executive Magistrate admitting the killings and injuries. The surviving daughter, a child witness, saw part of the assault. Nail clippings and blood samples were collected from the accused.
attempt_completion: Completed (three murders); Attempt (s.307 injuries to two children)
physical_harm: Three deaths: brother and wife died of head injuries (wife also burnt); son died after being shifted to hospital; two children injured
premeditation_planning: Court held no premeditation or pre-planning to eliminate the family; High Court had found the assault premeditated, but the Supreme Court found the High Court gave inadequate reasons
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness account of PW-7; testimony of neighbour PW-1 and landlord PW-3; post-mortem opinion of doctors PWs 6 and 11; recovery of stone inside house; accused's confessional statement to Executive Magistrate
witness_credibility: Found credible; no reason to disbelieve PW-7, PW-1 and PW-3; doctors' opinion accepted
post_offence_conduct: Accused gave a story of three thieves entering the house, which the High Court found false (as recited by the Supreme Court); accused's confession was recorded in hospital
custody_duration: In jail since 30.06.2001; in death cell since 03.05.2006; more than 10 years in jail and more than 5 years in death cell (as stated by the Court)
trial_duration: offence: 28.06.2001 (night intervening 28/29.06.2001); trial judgment: 04/05.03.2003; High Court: 03.05.2006; Supreme Court: 30.09.2011
legal_representation: Accused: Tara Chand Sharma, Mahabir Singh Mangla, Uma Datta, Kishan Datta, Neelam Sharma. State: Sushil Karanjkar, Sachin Patil, Sanjay Kharde, Sankar A Chillarge, Asha Gopalan Nair
investigation_status: FIR registered (Crime No. 41 of 2001); investigation completed; charge-sheet filed; trial completed in Sessions Court
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.302 and 307, life imprisonment and 7 years RI, s.201 acquitted. High Court: accused's appeal dismissed, State's appeal allowed, death sentence imposed. Supreme Court: conviction upheld; death sentence set aside; life imprisonment restored
prosecution_argument: Given three deaths and injuries to two members of one family, the death sentence awarded by the High Court was justified
defence_argument: Several mitigating circumstances were ignored; death penalty not warranted and the case is not rarest of rare
legal_principle_applied: Rarest of rare test; balancing of aggravating and mitigating circumstances; requirement that an appellate court give adequate and acceptable reasons for enhancing life sentence to death
precedent_relied_upon: Ajitsingh Hamamsingh Gujral v. State of Maharashtra, JT 2011 (10) SC 465 (distinguished); Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab, (1980) 2 SCC 684; Machhi Singh v. State of Punjab, (1983) 3 SCC 470; C. Muniappan v. State of Tamil Nadu, (2010) 9 SCC 567 (the last three referred to)
sentencing_rationale: High Court gave no adequate and acceptable reasons for death sentence; no pre-planning; unblemished antecedents; no dangerous weapon; not a menace to society; trial court's life sentence appropriate
judicial_mitigating_factors: No pre-planning; quarrel arose from land dispute; accused was sleeping with victims that night; no dangerous weapon used; unblemished antecedents; accused was 28 and jobless; long incarceration; no finding that accused cannot be reformed
judicial_aggravating_factors: Death of three persons (acknowledged by the Court); the Court did not endorse the High Court's other aggravating findings
